notes.front: What is a part 107 certificate of waiver?
notes.back: An FAA certificate authorising deviation from listed part 107 rules, issued when the FAA finds the operation can be conducted safely under its terms.
notes.explanation: The holder may deviate only as far as the certificate specifies and must meet any conditions or limitations in it.
notes.example: Like a planning permission for one project: it allows something the normal rules forbid, on stated conditions.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.200 Waiver policy and requirements (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: What is the § 107.205 list?
notes.back: The closed list of part 107 regulations from which a certificate of waiver may authorise deviation.
notes.explanation: Rules not on the list, such as the alcohol rule, cannot be waived under § 107.200.
notes.example: Like a menu: only the dishes on it can be ordered, however good the reason.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Which waivers will never be issued to allow carrying another person’s property for compensation or hire?
notes.back: Waivers of § 107.25 (operation from a moving vehicle or aircraft) and § 107.31 (visual line of sight).
notes.explanation: Both sections are waivable for other purposes, but not for property delivery for hire.
notes.example: A beyond-VLOS pipeline inspection may be waived; a beyond-VLOS parcel delivery for hire may not.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: What must a request for a certificate of waiver contain?
notes.back: A complete description of the proposed operation, and a justification showing it can safely be conducted under the waiver.
notes.explanation: The AC adds that supporting data should be proportional to the relief requested.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.200 Waiver policy and requirements (eCFR); FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.20.2
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: May the FAA attach its own limitations to a certificate of waiver?
notes.back: Yes; the Administrator may prescribe additional limitations, and the holder must comply with them.
notes.explanation: A waiver widens what is allowed only within its stated conditions.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.200 Waiver policy and requirements (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a certificate of waiver authorise deviation from § 107.25 (operation from a moving vehicle or aircraft)?
notes.back: Yes. It is on the § 107.205 list of regulations subject to waiver. Not, though, for carrying property for hire.
notes.explanation: It can allow flying from a moving land or water vehicle over a populated area, which § 107.25 otherwise limits to sparsely populated areas (AC ¶5.14.1).
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR); FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.14.1
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a certificate of waiver authorise deviation from § 107.29(a)(2) and (b) (anti-collision lighting at night and in civil twilight)?
notes.back: Yes. It is on the § 107.205 list of regulations subject to waiver.
notes.explanation: Only the lighting can be waived; the night training requirement in § 107.29(a)(1) is not on the list.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a certificate of waiver authorise deviation from § 107.31 (visual line of sight)?
notes.back: Yes. It is on the § 107.205 list of regulations subject to waiver. Not, though, for carrying property for hire.
notes.explanation: This is the waiver that allows beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights, but never for carrying another person’s property for hire.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a certificate of waiver authorise deviation from § 107.33 (visual observer)?
notes.back: Yes. It is on the § 107.205 list of regulations subject to waiver.
notes.explanation: The waiver’s own conditions can then replace § 107.33’s rules on communication and coordination between the visual observer and the crew.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a certificate of waiver authorise deviation from § 107.35 (operation of multiple small unmanned aircraft systems)?
notes.back: Yes. It is on the § 107.205 list of regulations subject to waiver.
notes.explanation: Without it, nobody may fly, or act as remote PIC or visual observer for, more than one unmanned aircraft at a time; this is how that can be allowed.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a certificate of waiver authorise deviation from § 107.37(a) (yielding the right of way)?
notes.back: Yes. It is on the § 107.205 list of regulations subject to waiver.
notes.explanation: Only paragraph (a) is listed; § 107.37(b), not flying so close as to create a collision hazard, cannot be waived.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a certificate of waiver authorise deviation from § 107.39 (operation over people)?
notes.back: Yes. It is on the § 107.205 list of regulations subject to waiver.
notes.explanation: It covers flight over people that none of § 107.39’s exceptions allows, such as by a drone that fits no subpart D category.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a certificate of waiver authorise deviation from § 107.41 (operation in certain airspace)?
notes.back: Yes. It is on the § 107.205 list of regulations subject to waiver.
notes.explanation: AC ¶5.10.2: a waiver, not an ATC authorization, is the route for pilots whose extra equipment (such as geofencing) is their safety case in controlled airspace.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR); FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.10.2
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a certificate of waiver authorise deviation from § 107.51 (operating limitations)?
notes.back: Yes. It is on the § 107.205 list of regulations subject to waiver.
notes.explanation: It can allow, for example, flight above 400 feet or in lower visibility, on the waiver’s own conditions.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a certificate of waiver authorise deviation from § 107.145 (operations over moving vehicles)?
notes.back: Yes. It is on the § 107.205 list of regulations subject to waiver.
notes.explanation: It can relax § 107.145’s conditions for flying over people inside moving vehicles, such as the closed-site or no-sustained-flight limits for Categories 1 to 3.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: How far ahead does the FAA encourage waiver applications, and how quickly does it aim to decide?
notes.back: At least 60 days before the operation; the FAA will strive to decide within 60 days.
notes.explanation: Neither period is a legal requirement, and complex requests may take longer.
notes.source: AC 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.20.2, Application Process

notes.front: Can the “sparsely populated area” condition for operating from a moving vehicle be waived?
notes.back: Yes, under §§ 107.200 and 107.205; VLOS and all other part 107 rules still apply.
notes.explanation: The waiver removes only the sparsely-populated condition.
notes.source: AC 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.14.1, Waiving the Sparsely-Populated Area Provision

notes.front: What happened to night waivers issued under the pre-2021 rules?
notes.back: Those issued before 16 March 2021 terminated on 17 May 2021; after that, none issued before 21 April 2021 may be used for night flight.
notes.explanation: Night flight now depends on § 107.29 itself, not on the old waivers.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.29 Operation at night (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: An operator asks for a waiver of § 107.27 (alcohol or drugs). Can one be issued?
notes.back: No. Section 107.27 is not on the § 107.205 list.
notes.explanation: Only listed regulations can be waived under § 107.200.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a certificate of waiver allow carriage of hazardous material under § 107.36?
notes.back: No. Section 107.36 is not on the § 107.205 list; carriage needs an exemption instead.
notes.explanation: An exemption under part 11 is a different process from a part 107 waiver.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Can a waiver let a remote PIC who has not done the post-April-2021 test or training fly at night?
notes.back: No. Only § 107.29(a)(2) and (b), the lighting requirements, are waivable; § 107.29(a)(1) is not.
notes.explanation: The waiver list names only the lighting paragraphs of § 107.29.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: Is § 107.37(b), operating so close to another aircraft as to create a collision hazard, waivable?
notes.back: No. Only § 107.37(a), yielding the right of way, is on the waiver list.
notes.explanation: A waiver can change who gives way, never permit a collision hazard.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: A company seeks a VLOS waiver to deliver customers’ parcels for payment beyond line of sight. What will the FAA do?
notes.back: Refuse: no § 107.31 waiver is issued for carrying another person’s property for compensation or hire.
notes.choices:
A) Issue it if the safety case is strong
B) Refuse it
C) Issue it only for daylight operations
notes.choicesExplained: A: no safety case can overcome the express bar in § 107.205(c). C: time of day does not matter; the bar is on carrying property for hire.
notes.explanation: The same bar applies to § 107.25 moving-vehicle waivers.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: A certificate of waiver lets a pilot fly beyond VLOS up to 200 feet. He flies beyond VLOS at 300 feet. Is that covered?
notes.back: No. A holder may deviate only to the extent the certificate specifies, and must meet its conditions and limitations.
notes.explanation: Outside the waiver’s terms, the normal part 107 rules apply in full.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.200 Waiver policy and requirements (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date

notes.front: A pilot needs to fly where § 107.41 requires prior ATC authorisation and wants credit for geo-fencing beyond part 107 requirements. What does the AC advise?
notes.back: Apply for a certificate of waiver; ATC authorisation decisions are not based on equipage beyond part 107.
notes.explanation: Extra equipage has not been certificated by the FAA and is examined case by case.
notes.source: AC 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.10.2, Air Traffic Organization (ATO)

notes.front: Which part of § 107.37 can be waived, and which cannot?
notes.back: Paragraph (a), yielding the right of way, can be waived; paragraph (b), not creating a collision hazard, cannot.
notes.explanation: The waiver list names § 107.37(a) only.
notes.contrast: (a) yielding: waivable. (b) collision hazard: never waivable.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 107.205 List of regulations subject to waiver (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 107 as of that date
